title: Machine learning-driven SERS platform for rapid detection and multi-analyte discrimination
content: Surface-enhanced Raman Scattering (SERS) has attracted considerable research attention owing to its outstanding capability for molecular identification, even at the single-molecule level. However, the selective identification of analyte molecules in real-world environments, such as in food and water sources, remains a significant challenge. In this study, we report the fabrication of a flexible, plasmonic nanopyramid array on a laminating polymer film using an inverted nanopyramid array on a silicon master mold. The performance of the fabricated silver (Ag) nanopyramid SERS substrate was characterized by using Rh6G as a probe molecule, reaching a limit of detection (LOD) down to 10−12 M with an analytical enhancement factor (EF) of 2.3 × 108. The RSD value of 9.9% at 1362 cm−1 was obtained for the intensity distribution across the substrate, showing robust uniformity and reproducibility. In addition, the detection of crystal violet (CV) and thiram was performed with a detection limit of 10−10 M and 10−8 M, respectively. Further, the detection of CV and thiram on a tomato's surface was successfully executed, demonstrating the substrate's flexibility and its practical applicability in real-world applications. Moreover, the discrimination of thiram, a fungicide, and CV, a model dye was carried out integrating with machine learning algorithms. Nine machine learning (ML) algorithms were executed to identify CV and thiram in their mixture. Among the algorithms employed, SVM attained a maximum cross-validation accuracy of 94.9% on an augmented dataset, and all classifiers correctly attributed every uniquely identifiable peak of CV and thiram. Thus, machine learning assisted SERS discrimination of multiple analytes has great potential for monitoring environment and human health.
